name: Pauline Hanson
role: Founder and leader of Pauline Hanson's One Nation; Member for Oxley (1996-1998); Senator for Queensland since 2016
summary: Right-wing populist and nationalist who built One Nation around sharply lower immigration, an end to multiculturalism, assimilation, opposition to special Indigenous programs, and hostility to Islam. She combines protectionism, curbs on foreign ownership, a sceptical stance on UN agreements and climate action, support for coal and nuclear power, firearms rights, and conservative social positions, with a free speech and referendum agenda against what she calls the political establishment. On economics she is pro-business on wages and welfare yet interventionist on tariffs, resource ownership and infrastructure.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Her party's plan is to strengthen Medicare: raise rebates so GPs bulk-bill, photo ID on cards and a fraud crackdown. She backs the public system rather than proposing to replace it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Asked about her record against minimum wage rises at the National Press Club (2026), she said businesses' ability to pay must be weighed and called for an industrial relations overhaul tipped back towards employers.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: she wants less red tape and business-friendlier labour rules, but also tariffs, a Commonwealth equity stake in oil and gas, and state-backed infrastructure.

public-ownership.rationale: Opposed the 1996 sale of Telstra as selling a profitable asset, and One Nation proposes a Commonwealth-owned vehicle holding up to 30 per cent of new oil and gas projects; she has not called for public ownership of whole industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: One Nation opposes returning death duties and wants a higher tax-free threshold and income splitting; the only call to tax more is aimed at multinationals paying their fair share, not wealthy individuals.

unions-good.rationale: Her 2026 platform pushes an overhaul of industrial relations law in business's favour; she has not spoken for unions as such.

cut-welfare.rationale: In 2016 she said welfare spending is out of control and must be reined in, warned it breeds dependency among those who have not worked for it, and proposed no extra payment for a second child.

surveillance-ok.rationale: In 2016 she called for monitoring mosques and schools and One Nation proposed CCTV in mosques on security grounds; also backed an ID card with chip, photo and fingerprint for services.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Her free speech policy would enshrine speech in the Constitution and repeal laws and bodies that restrict it; she also pledged to expel hate preachers, so evidence is not wholly one-way.

state-harmful.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

limit-guns.rationale: Her party opposes reclassification, ownership caps and buybacks and would repeal the post-Bondi gun laws; she opposed the government's 2025 post-Bondi restrictions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Backs raising defence spending to 5 per cent of GDP and says gun crime should face tougher enforcement; no direct statement on police powers or funding.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Mixed: in the 2017 Senate debate she said she had no problem with people marrying and that a civil ceremony would not worry Australians, argued it should have been a referendum, pushed celebrant exemptions, and abstained on the final vote.

abortion-legal.rationale: Her party's platform is pro-life and would cut the gestational limit and ban sex-selective abortion; she opposes abortion 'the day before birth' but supports it where the mother's life is at risk, so she stops short of a full ban.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: In 1996 she said she would not pay 'for something that happened over 200 years ago' and wanted ATSIC abolished; her 2026 policy abolishes the National Indigenous Australians Agency and treats all Australians equally 'not based on race'.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Introduced the Acknowledging Biological Reality Bill and at the 2026 Press Club described transgender ideology as an insurgency, quoting Germaine Greer that removing male anatomy does not make a woman.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Says Australians must live under one cultural umbrella and calls Australia a society that 'must be monocultural' (2026); 2016 maiden speech defends national identity and traditions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Called for a halt to further immigration in 1996 and 2016; her 2025 platform capped intake at 130,000 and in 2026 she called it an 'immigration catastrophe'.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Her budget plan withdraws from the UN, WHO and Paris Agreement; in 1996 she wanted to repudiate UN treaties and review UN membership.

free-trade.rationale: In her 2016 maiden speech she blamed the push for globalisation, economic rationalism and free trade for the country's decline; she calls for tariffs.

nation-first.rationale: Calls herself a patriot and unashamed nationalist who will put Australia and Australians first (2026); blamed globalisation in her 2016 speech.

open-borders.rationale: Said she should have a say on who comes into the country as she does in her own home, and wants immigration cut and borders tightened.

limit-growth.rationale: Says Paris targets are 'economic suicide' and told the 2026 Press Club the country must grow the national cake.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls climate change a hoax (Nov 2025, June 2026), wants to withdraw from the Paris Agreement and abolish the Climate Change department.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Her energy policy would repeal the nuclear ban and build a 1400 MW reactor on the east coast; she repeated support at the 2026 Press Club.

experts-over-public.rationale: Questions CSIRO and the IPCC and pushes a COVID royal commission to expose expert advice; says public decisions should be by citizens through referendums.

tax-inheritance.rationale: One Nation's tax policy, which she leads, states continued opposition to the reintroduction of death duties.

basic-income.rationale: Said welfare is 'not a right, unless you are aged or sick', which contradicts an unconditional payment to every adult.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In a media release she said One Nation has never had a problem with tariffs to protect Australian jobs, industries and sovereign capability and called for tariffs on steel imports.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Backs a Commonwealth equity stake in oil and gas projects, tariffs to keep steelmaking as a sovereign capability, and state-funded dams, rail and ports.

direct-votes.rationale: Her policy calls for citizen-initiated referendums so citizens can propose laws; she complained in 2016 that Australians were never allowed to vote on immigration and in 2017 that same-sex marriage should have been a referendum.

separate-church-state.rationale: Told the Senate in 2016 that government is secular, that separation of church and state is essential to freedom, and that sharia conflicts with it; she also calls Australia a Judaeo-Christian society.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Said Australia's Constitution prevents religious rule and that sharia law should not be acknowledged or allowed; she stressed the secular state.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Describes Australia as multiracial but insists on a single culture, welcoming migrants of all races who assimilate; the standard is cultural, not ethnic.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: In 1996 she objected to land and funds available only to Aboriginal people, native title spending and being told 'this is our land'; she wants the NIAA abolished.

conscription.rationale: In 1996 she called for 12 months' compulsory national service with some military training; in 2019 she opposed compelling young people into volunteer service.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Attacks out-of-control spending and debt interest (2016 and 2026) and runs a $90 billion savings plan to cut debt, though she also wants state-funded infrastructure to stimulate the economy.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Wants welfare and health services limited to people who prove entitlement, with an ID card for access, and criticises migrants collecting benefits; no explicit citizens-only rule found.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In 2016 she said welfare is not a right except for the aged and sick, backed stopping school leavers going straight onto welfare, and told people to 'get a job'.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Said in 1996 that Australia should not have 'one group enjoying one set of privileges' and when launching the Voice No campaign called race-based political power 'apartheid ... rightly consigned to the dustbin of history'.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Wants new coal-fired stations ('yes, in South Australia and Queensland'), cheaper coal and gas power and an ended net zero.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Said in 2016 that migrants who do not obey the law and respect the culture should leave, and praised those who assimilate; in 2026 said Australia must be monocultural.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: At the 2026 Press Club called the gender pay gap 'smoke and mirrors', attributing it to time out of work.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said in 2016 that politicians' perks and backroom deals go on while ordinary people suffer and in 2026 that Australians no longer buy 'this crap from the political establishment'.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Backs state-built dams and rail, tariffs, a Commonwealth oil and gas stake, an ID card and a national citizen-initiated referendum scheme.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says all Australians should be treated equally regardless of race, but has also voted against anti-discrimination protections for LGBTQ and intersex people.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: In 1996 said a truly multicultural country can never be strong or united; in 2026 called multiculturalism an 'utterly flawed' policy and asked how cohesion can arise when people cannot speak the language.

party-controls-media.rationale: Her free speech policy would dismantle censorship and speech regulation, and she says she wants unbiased independent reporting; she opposes government direction of information.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Introduced a bill in 2018 to lengthen the residence period for citizenship to eight years, double the government's proposal.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: In 2016 she attacked leaders for signing agreements giving away sovereignty and rejects supranational bodies such as the UN as expansionist.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: One Nation backs AUKUS and she wants defence spending lifted, and has urged Australia to join the US in its 2026 Iran war.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: At the 2026 Press Club she objected that under multiculturalism all cultures are 'allowed equivalence to ours', calling opposition to that common sense.

minority-language-support.rationale: Wants multiculturalism abolished, multicultural funding cut and SBS shut, and says citizens must speak English.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Wanted all foreign aid ceased in 1996 and her budget plan cuts it; at the 2026 Press Club she softened to support aid 'spent well' while putting Australians first and refusing money for countries close to China.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Said at the 2026 Press Club that the RBA is separate from the executive and that she would not try to influence its rate decisions, placing the onus on government spending.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Says climate policy should rest on repeatable evidence and rejects costly action on contested claims.

equal-parenting.rationale: Says children need both parents and wants fairer shared parenting and child support, but her policy page does not specify a presumption of equal time.

patriotic-education.rationale: Praised schools raising the flag and singing the anthem in 2016; her policy says classrooms should have no 'Western, white, gender, guilt shaming'.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Called in 1996 for equality for all Australians and objected to benefits available only to Aboriginal people; in 2026 said money should go to any Australian on individual need 'not based on race'.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Led the One Nation 'No' campaign to the Voice, saying it would give a minority more political power than the majority based on race.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Her party opposes removing colonial statues or changing the flag: 'hiding our history doesn't change it'.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: In 2016 raised male suicide linked to family breakdown and said family law is discriminatory against men; asked for equal treatment of fathers.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: In 2016 she said ports, utilities, water and farmland should not be sold to foreigners; her policy puts essential services off limits and writes a national-interest test.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Said she does not think foreigners should own Australian homes or farmland; her policy bans further freehold farmland sales to foreigners and stops property sales to non-residents.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said in 2016 that Australia needs a national government, not a corporate or union one, and that high immigration serves multinationals, banks and big business.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Proposed in 2016 that taxpayers support the first child only, with no increase in welfare for further children; she wants lower immigration but has not proposed birth incentives.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Pledged in 1996 to expose and repudiate UN treaties, criticised 'signing away our sovereignty', and her party says sovereignty must be protected from international organisations.

socialized-care.rationale: One Nation's family tax plan is meant to encourage parents to care for their own children and cut government childcare spending; at the 2026 Press Club she called childcare funding 'completely out of control'.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Introduced a bill to define sex in law and protect female-only spaces, which would not recognise gender identity, and pledged in 2026 to sack the Sex Discrimination Commissioner over trans policy.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Her 2016 maiden speech called Muslims bearers of a culture and ideology incompatible with Australia's; in 2026 she narrowed the target to radical Islam and 'places immersed in extremism', after a February remark that she apologised for.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Called for banning the burqa nationally on security grounds in 2016 and wore one in the Senate; a narrower rule on dress in state bodies was not addressed directly.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Wants defence spending raised to 5 per cent of GDP.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Supports AUKUS and close alignment with the United States and has called for Australia to back Trump's war effort.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Her bill 'acknowledges biological reality' and she says transgender women are not women.

farm-price-support.rationale: Strongly supports a federal-government-backed rural lending fund for farmers through drought; no price guarantees or public purchase proposed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Her 2018 bill demanded a real English test for citizenship, and in 2026 she cited people not speaking English at home as a threat to cohesion.

voter-id.rationale: Said she made voter ID legislation a condition of supporting the government's electoral bill and that the voter integrity bill would not exist without her.

close-ties-china.rationale: Called China's government an oppressive communist regime in 2016 and wanted to stop it owning Australian assets; in 2026 said 'we cannot disregard China' as a threat; has urged a boycott of Chinese goods.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Wants the NDIS means-tested and questions childcare and paid parental leave spending, while promising direct help to those doing it toughest.

national-resource-control.rationale: Her oil and gas policy says the resources belong to the Australian people and sets up direct Commonwealth ownership; in 2016 she said land, houses and companies should stay locally owned.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: In 1996 she said skin colour does not decide disadvantage and that welfare, not racism, was damaging Aboriginal people.

notes: Living person: no inference; evidence about a nearby question is left null. Several positions shifted: in 1996 she called for national service and a halt to Asian immigration, by 2016 the target was Muslim immigration, and in 2026 she framed it as radical Islam and 'monocultural' Australia; abortion shifted from pro-choice (1996) to a pro-life platform (2022); on foreign aid she moved from ceasing it (1996) to 'if spent well' (2026). The recent position is used. Party policy pages are treated as programs she leads and are medium unless she personally stated the position. theyvoteforyou.org.au sits behind a bot check, so her division record could not be read directly; vote-based answers rest on news reports and Hansard debate text.
